text:
Winnipeg played the better game and lost it at 3:21 of overtime, when JJ Peterka beat Stuart Skinner on a 14% chance to make it BOS 4, WPG 3. The Jets carried 3.63 expected goals to Boston's 3.19 and won 55% of the simulated replays, yet it was the Bruins who left with the points.

The scoring was odd from the start. Dylan DeMelo opened it for WPG on a 2% slap shot, and Mario Ferraro put the Jets up 3-2 with 8 seconds left in the second on a 1% wrist shot. Boston's goals were more honest. James Hagens made it 2-1 on a 35% chance, and Elias Lindholm tied it at 3-3 with a tip-in at 18:22 of the third, a 9% look. Kyle Connor scored on the power play and finished with 9 shots on goal, and the Jets were out-chanced only 2.61 to 1.96 at even strength, so the gap came from special teams. Winnipeg went 1 for 3 with the man advantage and created 1.44 expected goals there, while Boston went 0 for 2 on 0.27.

Jeremy Swayman saved about half a goal more than expected on 33 shots, with 30 saves on 3.47 expected goals against. Skinner allowed 4 on 3.19, nearly a goal worse than the chances he faced. Cole Perfetti had the best look that didn't go in, a 32% second-period chance that Swayman turned away. In a game this tight, that stop and the late tip-in separated the teams.
